failure.configuration: 100 measured echoes plus one readiness echo per size; diagnostic ErrorLog enabled, packet observer disabled; standalone Go concurrency was not recorded, unlike the instrumented observations which explicitly set GOMAXPROCS=4

interpretation: Late duplicate fragments can reopen incomplete split entries after completed assemblies are deleted [INFERENCE from wire observation and reference receiveSplitPacket source]; the traced successful run is not itself a reproduction of the limit failure. The observed failure and late duplicates occurred with Go peers only, so this evidence does not attribute the issue to tokio-raknet. The packet observer changes scheduling; no duplicate in one instrumented Rust-to-Go run does not prove duplicates are impossible.
reproduce: Set BENCH_TRACE_SPLITS=1, BENCH_TRACE_DIRECTION=go-to-go and BENCH_SPLIT_COUNT=100, then run go run . loopback --count 100 from tools/bench-compare/go; for Rust-to-Go run the same Go serve command and a Rust client with count 100 and TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS=4. Diagnostics are separate from timed rounds; the comparison runner disables the observer.
